title: Primate-specific regulation of the human glycosphingolipid gatekeeper UGCG.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: RCSB PDB (Protein Data Bank) full-text search for 'UGCG ceramide glucosyltransferase' returned exactly 8 entries (26QF, 26QG, 26QH, 26QI, 26QJ, 26QM, 26QS, 26QT); opened metadata for 26QF (apo human UGCG, 3.22 Å) and 26QM (UDP-glucose + phospholipid bound, 3.07 Å). Europe PMC: no PMCID, no open full text, no supplement, no text-mined accessions.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the structures are eight functional states at 2.9-3.4 Å, the primate-specific steric element, the metal-independent arginine mechanism, and the inhibitor-bound structures all come from the abstract only. Any enzyme-kinetics or mutagenesis tables are presumably in the paywalled supplement and were not seen.

a1_downloadable.note: Structures are public in PDB (8 entries verified via RCSB search); paper full text and supplement are paywalled and not retrievable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: This is a cryo-EM (cryogenic electron microscopy) structural paper; there is no table of measured outcomes per item. Any label (e.g. activity of mutants) would sit in an unseen paywalled supplement, likely a handful of mutants.

a3_inputs_present.note: Atomic coordinates and the UGCG sequence are present in the PDB entries.

a4_units_stated.note: No measured-quantity table was accessible, so no units can be checked.

a5_enough_rows.note: Eight structures of one protein (verified count in PDB); any mutant kinetics would be tens of rows at most, far under the 400-row minimum.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Tiny, but irrelevant given no modellable table.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 8 PDB entries match the abstract's 'eight functional states'.

a8_label_provenance.note: Structures are experimental measurements; no model-derived labels involved, but no label exists to trace.

backbone.name: ESM-2, a protein language model (not applicable: one protein)

integration.partner_dataset: ChEMBL inhibitor bioactivities for UGCG (glucosylceramide synthase) could be joined by UniProt Q16739, but that is a separate project not built on this paper's data.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: None from this paper's data alone; it contributes 8 structures of one enzyme.

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim is supportable: the data are eight cryo-EM structures of a single human enzyme.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the structure of a lipid-making enzyme to predict how strongly drugs or mutations change its activity.
plain_idea.train_on: Eight experimentally solved 3D structures of one human enzyme (UGCG), in different bound states; 8 examples verified in the Protein Data Bank.
plain_idea.predict: Enzyme activity or inhibitor potency, which would have to come from lab assays in the paper's paywalled supplement (not seen).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Drug developers targeting glycosphingolipid storage diseases could prioritise inhibitors, but eight structures of one protein cannot train a model.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper: a structural biology study yielding 8 PDB entries of one enzyme. The structures could serve as docking templates for a ChEMBL-based UGCG inhibitor project, but that would be a different dataset.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; no modellable table exists.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count PDB entries for UGCG: 8 (done, kills it).

verdict_reason: Cryo-EM structure paper: only 8 PDB structures of one enzyme (verified in RCSB), no outcome table in accessible data, paywalled supplement; fails A2 (no label column) and A5 (8 rows).
